mainTopic: Challenges to רב הונא's view that for רבי יוסי parts of a קרבן are תרי גופי for פיגול: the two loaves, רב אשי's ברייתא, and רבינא's מנחה case
overview: The גמרא is testing רב הונא's view that, for רבי יוסי, two parts of a קרבן (like the right and left thighs) are תרי גופי, two separate bodies, so a פיגול intention about one does not spread to the other. First it asks how, if that is so, intentions about half a כזית from each of the two loaves could combine. רב הונא assigns that source to רבי, but the גמרא asks which view רבי follows, and the difficulty returns. The גמרא tries reading the ברייתא as 'both lambs' so that it fits the רבנן and rejects רבי מאיר. But the strong word 'לעולם' shows the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, so the problem stands. Next, רב אשי's ברייתא in the name of רבי יוסי shows that an intention about pouring the leftover blood makes the meat פיגול. By קל וחומר, an intention about one thigh should surely make the other thigh פיגול. רבינא then starts a parallel קל וחומר from a מנחה: an intention about burning the קומץ makes the שיריים פיגול. That argument finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: If they are two bodies, how can they combine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רב הונא: if רבי יוסי holds the parts are תרי גופי, intentions about each loaf should not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say they are two separate bodies, would they combine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רב הונא. If רבי יוסי treats the two loaves as two separate bodies, how could an earlier source say that half-olive-bulk intentions about each one join together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining two halves into one כזית only makes sense if both items count as one unit. If they are תרי גופי, each half stays on its own, and half a כזית is too small to make פיגול. So the source that lets them combine seems to show that רבי יוסי treats them as one body.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate bodies, meaning two independent units, not one
They combine, joining together to reach the needed amount
A קרבן made unfit by the intention, while doing the service, to eat it after its allowed time

phrases.english: But if you say
they are two bodies,
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's claim about רבי יוסי: two parts like the right and left thighs count as separate units.

phrases.english: would they combine?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ תְּרֵי גּוּפֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge, begun on the previous amud, against רב הונא's reading of רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that for רבי יוסי the parts are תרי גופי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source lets half-olive-bulk intentions about two loaves combine. Combining requires one unit, so the loaves cannot be two separate bodies.

steps.title: The source follows רבי, not רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the combining source follows רבי, and he brings a ברייתא where רבי rules that two half-olive-bulk intentions keep the קרבן valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי's. As it is taught: if someone slaughters one lamb intending to eat half a כזית from this loaf, and the other lamb intending to eat half a כזית from that loaf, רבי says: I say this is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back: the source that lets the halves combine is not רבי יוסי at all. It follows רבי, and he quotes a ברייתא with רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the source belongs to רבי, it proves nothing about רבי יוסי, so the challenge falls away. In רבי's case, each lamb was slaughtered with intent about half a כזית of a different loaf, and רבי rules the offering is כשר. The two halves did not combine there.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way of assigning a source to a specific תנא
A lamb, here one of the two lambs brought with the loaves on שבועות
Half an olive-bulk, less than the minimum needed for פיגול
Valid, not disqualified

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is רבי,
phrases.notes: "This" means the earlier source where the halves combined.

phrases.english: as it is taught: One who slaughters the lamb
to eat half an olive-bulk from this loaf,
and similarly its fellow,
to eat half an olive-bulk from that loaf,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁזֶּה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: I say that this is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by moving the source away from רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The combining source reflects רבי יוסי, which would show the loaves are one body for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source reflects רבי, so it says nothing about רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: For רבי, halves combine only if he said "from both"
steps.stepSummary: From the exact wording of רבי's case, רב הונא infers that רבי does let intentions combine when the person said "a כזית from both of them."
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it is valid is that he said "half" and "half." But if he said "a כזית from both of them," it combines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא reads closely into רבי's ruling. The offering stayed valid only because each intention was a separate "half," while one intention about a כזית from both loaves together would combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the earlier combining source to רבי: in that case the person must have spoken of a כזית from both loaves together. So רבי can hold both rulings. Separate half-intentions stay apart, but one intention covering both loaves adds up to a כזית and makes פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason. It is used to infer what would happen in the opposite case
An olive-bulk, the minimum amount that counts for פיגול
From both of them, meaning both loaves together

phrases.english: The reason is that he said "half, half,"
but if he said "an olive-bulk from both of them"
it combines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by showing from רבי's wording that he allows combining in the right case.
steps.raayaObject: That the combining source matches רבי's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A close reading of רבי's ruling in the ברייתא: it stays valid only because he said "half, half"
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, two separate half-olive-bulk intentions keep the קרבן valid. One intention about "a כזית from both" combines and makes it פיגול.

steps.title: Whose view does רבי follow? The difficulty returns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view רבי follows. Under the רבנן even one loaf should be enough, and under רבי יוסי the original difficulty comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, whose view does he follow? If he follows the רבנן, then even intent about one of the loaves should be enough! If he follows רבי יוסי, our difficulty returns to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer by asking which side of the משנה's argument רבי belongs to. Either way there is a problem, and the original question comes right back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that פיגול intent about one loaf ruins both, so there is no need to combine anything: one loaf alone works. If רבי follows רבי יוסי, then רבי יוסי also lets the two loaves combine. That again suggests they are one body, against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose view? Asking which side of a dispute someone follows
Even with just one of them as well
Our difficulty returns to its place, meaning the original question is back

steps.confusionAlert: Moving the source to רבי did not solve anything by itself. Since רבי must follow either the רבנן or רבי יוסי, the problem with רבי יוסי can come back.

phrases.english: And Rabbi, according to whom?
If according to the Rabbis,
even with one of them as well!
If according to Rabbi Yosei,
our difficulty returns to its place.
phrases.notes: Back to the question in step 1: if they are two bodies, how can they combine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of steps 2–3 by showing that assigning the source to רבי does not escape the problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that the combining source follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי follows the רבנן, combining is unnecessary because one loaf is enough. If he follows רבי יוסי, then רבי יוסי allows combining, which brings back the challenge from step 1.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא pattern: when an answer moves a source to another תנא, the גמרא checks whether that תנא fits either side of the main dispute.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as 'both lambs' so it fits the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling follows the רבנן. It rereads the ברייתא as 'בשניהן', which means both lambs, so an intention about even one loaf is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it follows the רבנן. Don't read 'until he has פיגול intent about both of them' as the loaves. Read it as both of them, the lambs. Then the intention can be about even one of the loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4 by changing one word in the ברייתא. Now the ברייתא fits the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was this: under the רבנן, an intention about one loaf should be enough, so why does the ברייתא require 'both'? The answer: 'both' does not mean both loaves. It means both lambs. You must slaughter both lambs with the פיגול intent, but that intent can be about just one loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: 'really, actually.' The גמרא uses it to go back to its first idea.
'With both of them' in the feminine form, meaning the two loaves.
'With both of them' in the masculine form, meaning the two lambs.

phrases.english: Actually, it is according to the Rabbis,
and do not say "until he has פיגול intent with both of them (the loaves)",
rather say "until he has פיגול intent with both of them (the lambs)",
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. The whole answer turns on switching from the feminine שתיהן to the masculine שניהן.

phrases.english: and even if the intent was about just one of them (the loaves).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4's question about which view רבי follows by rereading one word of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Both' meant both loaves, which clashes with the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Both' means both lambs. Intent about one loaf is enough, which fits the רבנן.

steps.title: What the ברייתא comes to reject: רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: On this reading, the ברייתא's point is to reject רבי מאיר, who says a פיגול intention during half of the מתיר works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to reject רבי מאיר, who says you can make something פיגול with half of the permitting act. It teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining why the ברייתא needed to say 'both lambs' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that slaughtering just one lamb with the bad intent is enough to make the loaves פיגול. By requiring both lambs, the ברייתא tells us that half of the מתיר does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To exclude,' meaning to reject a certain opinion.
Half of the act that permits the קרבן, like slaughtering only one of the two lambs.
'It teaches us': the new point being made.

phrases.english: And it comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Meir,
who says: one can make it פיגול through half of the permitting factor,
phrases.notes: Here the two lambs together are the 'מתיר' for the loaves, so slaughtering one lamb is the 'half.'

phrases.english: it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 5's answer by naming the opinion the ברייתא rejects.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא requires both lambs so that it rejects רבי מאיר's view about חצי מתיר.

steps.title: The word 'never' fits only if the ברייתא rejects two views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The ברייתא's strong word 'לעולם' makes sense if it follows רבי יוסי and rejects both רבי מאיר and the רבנן. If it rejects only רבי מאיר, why say 'never'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is 'never' doing there? It makes sense if the ברייתא means both loaves and both lambs, following רבי יוסי. Then it rejects both רבי מאיר and the רבנן, and that is why it says 'never.' But if it follows the רבנן and rejects only רבי מאיר, what is 'never' for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from steps 5 and 6. It points to the ברייתא's emphatic word 'לעולם.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: An emphatic 'never' suggests the ברייתא is rejecting more than one opinion. Under רבי יוסי, you need both loaves and both lambs, which rejects רבי מאיר and the רבנן together. Under the new reading, it rejects only רבי מאיר, so the strong word seems out of place. This pushes the ברייתא back toward רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': it opens a challenge to what was just said.
'Granted': it sets up the side that works before showing the side that doesn't.
'That is why it says': this explains the wording.

steps.confusionAlert: 'לעולם' shows up with two jobs. In step 5 it is the גמרא's own word, meaning 'actually.' Here the גמרא is asking about the ברייתא's word 'לעולם,' which means 'never.'
steps.whyThisMatters: If the ברייתא must follow רבי יוסי, the original difficulty against רב הונא from step 1 stands unresolved.

phrases.english: If so, what is the meaning of "never"?
Granted, if you say it means both loaves and both lambs,
and it is the view of Rabbi Yosei,
and it comes to exclude both Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis,
that is why it says "never."
But if you say it follows the Rabbis,
and it comes to exclude only Rabbi Meir,
what is "never" for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of steps 5 and 6 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows the רבנן and rejects only רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The emphatic 'לעולם' suggests the ברייתא rejects two views. That fits רבי יוסי, not the רבנן.

steps.title: A further problem: רב אשי's ברייתא from רבי in the name of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another difficulty by recalling the ברייתא רב אשי brought. In it, רבי, speaking for רבי יוסי, says a פיגול intention about a thing done 'outside' works, but one about a thing done 'inside' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רב אשי say: Come and hear. רבי says in the name of רבי יוסי: if he had a פיגול intention about something done outside, the offering is פיגול. If it was about something done inside, it is not פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another challenge to רב הונא's view that, for רבי יוסי, an intention about one thigh does not spread to the other. It recalls a ברייתא that רב אשי used, and this sets up an argument that lands in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 left the first challenge to רב הונא standing, because the ברייתא must follow רבי יוסי. Now the word 'ועוד' adds a separate attack on רב הונא. The גמרא will study this ברייתא's details and build a קל וחומר from them (step 14).

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It introduces an additional difficulty.
Outside (in the courtyard) / inside (in the היכל, the Sanctuary).

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'outside' does not mean outside the Temple. It means the courtyard, compared with the inside of the היכל where the blood of these special offerings is sprinkled.

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't רב אשי say:
Come and hear:
רבי says in the name of רבי יוסי:
If he had a פיגול intention about a thing done outside, he has made it פיגול;
phrases.notes: This is about the bulls and goats that are burned, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל.

phrases.english: about a thing done inside, he has not made it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 leaves the first challenge to רב הונא unresolved, this adds a further, independent challenge to רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that for רבי יוסי a פיגול intention about the right thigh does not make the left thigh פיגול (the parts are תרי גופי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב אשי's ברייתא, which רבי teaches in the name of רבי יוסי, an intention about the blood makes the meat פיגול. By קל וחומר (step 14), an intention about one thigh should make the other thigh פיגול, against רב הונא.

steps.title: The ברייתא's examples where the offering is not פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives two examples where there is no פיגול. In the first, he stands outside and intends to do an inside act tomorrow. In the second, he stands inside and intends to do outside acts tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he stood outside and said, 'I slaughter in order to sprinkle its blood tomorrow,' it is not פיגול, because the intention was outside about an inside act. If he stood inside and said, 'I sprinkle in order to burn the parts tomorrow and pour the leftover blood tomorrow,' it is not פיגול, because the intention was inside about outside acts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains its rule with examples. In each of these two cases there is a 'mismatch', and the intention does not create פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on matching places. An intention counts only when the place where he stands and does the act matches the place of the act he is thinking about. Slaughtering happens outside but sprinkling happens inside, so that is a mismatch. Sprinkling happens inside but burning and pouring happen outside, so that is also a mismatch.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of; in order to.
To sprinkle (the blood).
The parts of the offering that are burned on the altar.
The leftover blood, poured out at the base of the altar.

phrases.english: How so?
If he was standing outside and said:
"I hereby slaughter with the intention
to sprinkle its blood tomorrow" — he has not made it פיגול,
because it is an intention outside about a thing done inside.
If he was standing inside and said:
"I hereby sprinkle with the intention
to burn the sacrificial parts tomorrow
and to pour out the leftover blood tomorrow" — he has not made it פיגול,
because it is an intention inside about a thing done outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the ברייתא's general rule from Step 8 through examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention made in one place about an act done in the other place does not create פיגול.

steps.title: The ברייתא's example where the offering is פיגול
steps.stepSummary: If he stands outside, slaughtering, and intends to pour the leftover blood and burn the parts tomorrow, the offering is פיגול. Both the intention and the acts are outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood outside and said, 'I slaughter in order to pour the leftover blood tomorrow and burn the parts tomorrow,' it is פיגול, because the intention was outside about an outside act.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the case that does work. Here the places match, so the intention creates פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering, pouring the leftover blood, and burning the parts all happen outside, in the courtyard. Because the places match, this intention counts. This case is the one the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: To pour out.
To burn on the altar.

phrases.english: If he was standing outside and said:
"I hereby slaughter with the intention
to pour out the leftover blood tomorrow
and to burn the sacrificial parts tomorrow" — he has made it פיגול,
because it is an intention outside about a thing done outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ, וְאָמַר: הֲרֵינִי שׁוֹחֵט עַל מְנָת לִשְׁפּוֹךְ שִׁירַיִים לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching case, the opposite of the two mismatched cases in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention outside about acts done outside (pouring the leftover blood, burning the parts) creates פיגול.

steps.title: What becomes פיגול from intending to pour the leftover blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in the case of intending to pour the leftover blood tomorrow, what is it that becomes פיגול?
steps.simpleTranslation: "To pour out the leftover blood": what would that make פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to examine the ברייתא's last case. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intention to pour blood is about the blood. So the גמרא wants to know which item that intention could actually make פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: To make what into פיגול?

phrases.english: "To pour out the leftover blood":
to make what פיגול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case just stated in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item becomes פיגול through an intention to pour the leftover blood tomorrow.

steps.title: It can't be the blood, because blood doesn't carry פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first possible answer, that the blood itself becomes פיגול. A משנה lists blood among the items for which there is no פיגול liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the blood becomes פיגול: does blood become פיגול? But we learned in a משנה: these are the things for which one is not liable because of פיגול: the קומץ, the frankincense, the incense, the priests' meal offering, the meal offering of the libations, the anointed כהן's meal offering, and the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the blood is what becomes פיגול. Then it immediately rules this out with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול liability applies to things that are permitted by something else, such as meat that becomes permitted once the blood is sprinkled. The משנה lists items that are not like that, and blood is on the list. So an intention to pour the leftover blood must be making something else פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a meal offering and burned.
Frankincense.
The incense.
The meal offering brought with the wine libations.
The anointed כהן גדול.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable because of פיגול' does not mean these items can never become invalid. It means one who eats them does not receive the punishment of פיגול.

phrases.english: If you say: to make the blood פיגול —
does blood become פיגול?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל:
phrases.english: These are the things for which one is not liable because of פיגול:
the handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of libations,
the meal offering of the anointed priest, and the blood!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לְאִיפַּגּוֹלֵי דָּם – דָּם מִי מִיפַּגַּל? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries one answer to Step 11's question and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the blood is what becomes פיגול through the intention to pour the leftover blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה lists blood among the items that carry no פיגול liability, so the blood cannot be what becomes פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: Ruling out the blood forces the גמרא to look for what else this intention affects. That search will decide how the ברייתא is read.

steps.title: The meat is what becomes פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Since the blood itself cannot become פיגול, the only option left is that the meat of the offering becomes פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the meat is what becomes פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from Step 11. It says the meat is what becomes פיגול when he intends to pour the leftover blood tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 ruled out the blood, because blood is on the list of things that carry no פיגול liability. The meat is the only option left. This answer sets up the קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
To become פיגול
The meat of the offering

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: it is the meat that becomes piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the remaining option after Step 12 rejected the blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What becomes פיגול when he intends to pour the leftover blood tomorrow?

steps.title: If an intention about the blood spreads to the meat, an intention about one thigh should spread to the other
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר. רבי יוסי makes the meat פיגול even though the intention was not about the meat. So an intention about the right thigh, which is part of the offering itself, should surely make the left thigh פיגול too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think it through. There, he had no intention about the meat itself, yet רבי יוסי said it becomes פיגול. Here, his intention is about the offering itself. Surely if he made the right thigh פיגול, he made the left thigh פיגול as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses Step 13 to build a קל וחומר. It attacks the view that a פיגול intention about one thigh does not spread to the other thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the intention was about the blood, and it still made the meat פיגול. In the thigh case, the intention is directly about a piece of the animal's own meat. If even an intention that was not about the meat at all spreads to the meat, an intention about part of the meat should certainly spread to the rest of it.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; the closing words of a קל וחומר
The right thigh
The left thigh
Itself

steps.whatToRemember: Pattern: X cannot become פיגול, so Y must be what becomes פיגול. That gives a קל וחומר that a פיגול intention spreads across the whole offering.

phrases.english: Now, if there,
where he had no intention about the meat itself,
Rabbi Yosei said it becomes piggul,
then here, where he had an intention about the offering itself,
is it not all the more so

phrases.aramaic: דְּפִיגֵּל בְּיֶרֶךְ יָמִין פִּיגֵּל בְּיֶרֶךְ שְׂמֹאל?
phrases.english: that if he made the right thigh piggul, he made the left thigh piggul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer in Step 13 into a קל וחומר challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that, for רבי יוסי, a פיגול intention about the right thigh makes only that thigh פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: an intention not about the meat at all makes the meat פיגול, so an intention about part of the meat should surely spread to all of it.

steps.title: רבינא's second challenge from the קומץ of a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another challenge from רבינא. Our משנה says that if he takes the קומץ intending to eat the שיריים or burn the קומץ tomorrow, רבי יוסי agrees the offering is פיגול and carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רבינא say: Come and hear. If someone takes the handful from a מנחה intending to eat its remainder, or to burn its handful, tomorrow, רבי יוסי agrees in this case that he made it פיגול, and one who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the same view. It quotes a משנה that רבינא used, and is setting up the same kind of argument as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the focus is the case of intending to burn the קומץ tomorrow. רבי יוסי agrees this makes the offering פיגול. The next steps ask what exactly becomes פיגול, exactly as was done with the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes the קומץ (the handful) from a מנחה
Its remainder, which the כהנים eat
Agrees, even though he disagrees elsewhere
Spiritual cutting off; the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Ravina say: Come and hear:
One who takes the handful from the meal offering
intending to eat its remainder
or to burn its handful, tomorrow:
Rabbi Yosei agrees in this case that he made it piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel challenge to the one finished in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that, for רבי יוסי, a פיגול intention about one thigh does not spread to the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a parallel קל וחומר from the case of a מנחה.

steps.title: What becomes פיגול when he intends to burn the קומץ tomorrow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the מנחה becomes פיגול in the case of intending to burn the קומץ tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of intending to burn its handful tomorrow, what is it that becomes פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a focused question about one case in the משנה. This is setup for the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same question as Step 11, now asked about a מנחה. The answer will decide whether the קל וחומר works.

keyTerms.meaning: Its handful

phrases.english: When he intends to burn its handful,
what is it that becomes piggul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case quoted in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the מנחה becomes פיגול: the קומץ or the שיריים?

steps.title: The קומץ itself cannot become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the קומץ becomes פיגול. A משנה lists the קומץ among the items that carry no פיגול liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the handful becomes פיגול, does a handful even become פיגול? But we learned in a משנה: These are the items for which one is not liable for פיגול: the handful, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the first possible answer by quoting a משנה. This matches how it ruled out the blood in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explicitly lists the קומץ, just as it lists the blood, among the items with no פיגול liability. So the intention about burning the קומץ cannot be making the קומץ itself פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
One is not liable for them because of פיגול

phrases.english: If you say the handful becomes piggul,
does a handful become piggul?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל:
phrases.english: These are the items for which one is not liable because of piggul:
phrases.notes: זבחים 42b; the same משנה the גמרא used for the blood in Step 12.

phrases.english: the handful, etc.!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the קומץ becomes פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly lists the קומץ among the items with no פיגול liability.

steps.title: The שיריים are what become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Since the קומץ cannot become פיגול, the שיריים must be what becomes פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the remainder is what becomes פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 16. It says the שיריים are what become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 13 exactly. The intention was about the קומץ, yet the שיריים become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: it is the remainder that becomes piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the remaining option after Step 17 rejected the קומץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What becomes פיגול when he intends to burn the קומץ tomorrow?

steps.title: Starting the קל וחומר from the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the same קל וחומר: there, he had no intention about the שיריים themselves. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think it through. There, he had no intention about the remainder itself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building the second קל וחומר, matching Step 14. The sentence continues onto the next amud, where the argument is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The intention was only about burning the קומץ, not about the שיריים, yet the שיריים become פיגול. The conclusion will follow the same pattern as Step 14. An intention about one thigh should surely spread to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if...; the opening words of a קל וחומר
Had an intention about

phrases.english: Now, if there,
where he had no intention about the remainder itself,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a קל וחומר on Step 18, in parallel to Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a פיגול intention about one thigh does not spread to the other thigh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר (still being built): an intention not about the שיריים makes them פיגול, so an intention about part of the offering should surely spread to all of it.
